none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

results.references: - Martin Zinkevich. [Online Convex Programming and Generalized Infinitesimal Gradient Ascent](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~brecht/cs294docs/week1/03.Zinkevich.pdf). 2003 (ICML). Complexity: $O(T)$ exact-gradient oracle calls, one per round, for deterministic regret $O(DG\sqrt{T})$ using Greedy Projection; its proved bound is $D^2/(2\eta_T)+(G^2/2)\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t$, giving $DG\sqrt{T}$ with $\eta_t=D/(G\sqrt{T})$. Equivalently, $O(1+D^2G^2/\varepsilon^2)$ calls suffice for average regret at most $\varepsilon>0$.

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Online convex optimization with an arbitrary sequence of differentiable losses f_t, each convex on the same nonempty compact convex set K. No strong convexity or Lipschitz-gradient assumption.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: At round t, choose x_t in K before receiving exactly ∇f_t(x_t). The reply depends on history only through its length and is independent of the oracle seed. Execution makes exactly T gradient calls, with no additional initialization calls. Public information is d, K, x0, D, G, T; the loss sequence is hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/OnlineConvexBoundedGradient.lean: Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Instance, spec.Query, spec.admissible; LongTails/TemplateOnline.lean: OnlineConvergence; LongTails/Template.lean: executeWithTrace and _run.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: K is a subset of Euclidean R^d, with d a natural number, using the Euclidean norm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Known positive bounds D and G satisfy diam(K) ≤ D and ‖∇f_t(x)‖ ≤ G for every t and x in K. The positive integer horizon T is known. Losses need not obey any distributional or temporal regularity assumption.

accuracy.label: deterministic
accuracy.details: The regret inequality must hold for every combined algorithm/oracle seed ω and every comparator u, not merely in expectation or almost surely.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/OnlineConvexBoundedGradient.lean: spec.successful explicitly quantifies ∀ ω and ∀ u.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: Static cumulative regret: for every u in K, ∑_{t=0}^{T−1}[f_t(x_t)−f_t(u)] ≤ DG√T. Equivalently, average regret is at most DG/√T. Accuracy concerns the entire query trace; the terminal output is Unit.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/OnlineConvexBoundedGradient.lean: spec.successful and spec.Output; supplied budget for OracleTemplate.OnlineGradientDescent.result; LongTails/TemplateOnline.lean: OnlineConvergence.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Standard finite-dimensional online convex optimization with bounded gradients, a bounded convex decision set, exact gradient feedback, and static regret. Local implementation and proof verification were not checked; the literature match concerns only the supplied setup and bound.
